# Common English verbs, base forms: a hand-compiled list for NeuroSciFi's evidence guard (webcortex/reasoning.py,
# _verb_bases and _verbs). Beside weak evidence a capitalised word at a clause head that is one of these, or one of
# their -s/-ed/-ing forms (generated by rule in code), is read as a verb, never as a name (the round-9 negative
# oracle). Words are separated by spaces and new lines; lines starting with "#" are comments. Over-inclusion only
# rejects more sentences beside weak evidence; a verb missing here can open a sentence as if it were a name.
